sentences.text: North Access Scanner validates each presented credential against current access authorization before enabling controlled entry.
The scanner accepts only credentials that can be read reliably and associated with an identifiable person.
The person presents the credential at the controlled entry point and waits for the scanner response.
The scanner checks that the authorization is active for the scheduled work period.
It also checks that the requested access area is within the person's approved scope.
An authorization that is expired, suspended, or incomplete results in a denied entry decision.
The gate remains secured when the scanner cannot verify a credential or retrieve the required authorization information.
A denial directs the person to contact the Field Supervisor or the HSE Officer for review.
Neither a verbal request nor a manually presented credential image overrides a scanner denial.
Approved entry is granted only after all configured identity and authorization checks pass.
Each attempt receives a unique transaction identifier for later reference.
The transaction records the credential identifier, decision time, access point, and decision outcome.
It also records the authorization version and the rule that determined the outcome.
The audit record distinguishes a rejected credential from an authorization that lacks the required scope.
The system retains successful and unsuccessful attempts under the site's access record retention policy.
Access records are protected against unauthorized alteration and are available to authorized reviewers.
The Field Supervisor reviews unusual denial patterns and unresolved access exceptions during the work shift.
The HSE Officer can use the recorded entry history to support personnel accountability during an incident.
If the scanner is unavailable, personnel follow the approved contingency process rather than bypassing the gate.
The contingency process requires a named approver and a recorded reason for any temporary access decision.
Temporary decisions are reconciled against the normal access record when scanner service is restored.
The scanner displays a clear outcome without exposing unnecessary personal information to people nearby.
Operators verify the scanner clock and connectivity during routine readiness checks.
Changes to access rules are controlled and reviewed before they become effective at the entry point.
This control provides a consistent basis for admitting authorized personnel and explaining each access decision.
